summary.en: The Education Bureau today held the annual sharing session for students and graduates awarded the Belt and Road Scholarship, attended by Under Secretary for Education Jeff Sze and Commissioner for Belt and Road Nicholas Ho, with over 100 awardees now pursuing development in Hong Kong. summary.en: An Air Niugini flight from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea made a safe emergency landing in the southern Philippines after a suspected engine fire. summary.en: Protests and strikes have hit several European countries, with demonstrators demanding more public service spending, higher wages and less defence spending, disrupting transport, health and education services. In Germany, protests broke out in several cities on Friday against the restoration of conscription and cuts to education funding; about 4,500 people marched in Berlin, where police deployed around 1,600 officers. In London, protesters gathered at Parliament Square and Trafalgar Square against military expansion and the rising cost of living, and police arrested several people. summary.en: The Hong Kong government has signed two agreements with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, formally establishing an AIIB office in Hong Kong. Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the office is a resounding vote of confidence in Hong Kong as an international financial centre, noting the city manages more than US$5 trillion in assets and can contribute directly to the bank's work. Hong Kong will inject a further US$20 million into the AIIB's Project Preparation Special Fund, taking total contributions to US$30 million, to help more developing member economies turn infrastructure plans into bankable projects. summary.en: Hong Kong Customs has cracked a case involving the sale of counterfeit goods through an online shop and a distribution centre, seizing about 800 items including unlicensed perfume and designer toys with an estimated market value of around HK$500,000. A 61-year-old man was arrested over suspected handling of criminal proceeds of up to HK$6 million. Acting on a tip-off, Customs raided an industrial unit in Kwun Tong on November 11 and seized the suspected items. The arrested local man is an employee of the online shop, responsible for daily storage and dispatch at the distribution centre, and is on police bail pending further investigation. The shop is run by a 30-year-old local man, the arrested man's son and the alleged mastermind, who has been out of Hong Kong for a long time. Customs said the counterfeit perfume is highly convincing and hard for ordinary consumers to tell apart, advising the public to check whether the label on a genuine bottle is centred and whether the engraving on the base is clear and neat. The seller set up its own website and social media accounts to pose as a large-scale online retailer and falsely claimed the goods came from overseas agents. The counterfeit perfume cost HK$100 to HK$200 to make and sold for about HK$700 to HK$1,000, roughly 80 per cent of the genuine price. Customs described the warehouse conditions as poor, posing a possible health risk to users, and said perfume samples will be sent to the Government Laboratory for safety testing, urging the public to shop at reputable stores.

summary.en: Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said the Government will push to pass a half-tax concession for physical commodity trading within this year, as part of efforts to turn Hong Kong into a hub for commodity and green fuel trading. Writing in her blog, Chan said the dedicated task force set up during Maritime Week to develop a green marine fuel trading platform will speed up work with the industry to build a global, diverse and open platform and expand green energy and shipping corridor networks. She said she has been in regular contact with the maritime and port industry to promote a series of tax concessions introduced since the 2020/21 tax year, and the industry is keen to use commodity trading to grow Hong Kong's maritime community. The Taxation (Amendment) (Tax Concessions for Shipping-related Activities and Physical Commodity Trading) Bill 2026, which supports the plan, will resume its second reading at the Legislative Council next Wednesday. Chan said a consultant's rough estimate puts the annual economic benefit of the half-tax concession at about HK$4.6 billion, while also helping attract more commodity trading activity to Hong Kong.

summary.en: Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law said she is confident Hong Kong will attract more international superstars to perform in the city in future. Speaking on a radio programme, Law said organisers can book the Hong Kong Coliseum a year in advance, while bookings at Kai Tak Sports Park already extend to 2028. On the difficulty of getting concert tickets, Law said many organisers offer ticket-and-hotel packages with the travel industry, but many fans only want tickets, so an anti-bot ticketing system has been adopted to help them buy. On whether a real-name ticketing system should be introduced, Law said some organisers have tried it, but checking identity cards and issuing wristbands at the door created a heavy burden, and the public should think carefully about whether they want that. summary.en: The Government plans to amend the Buildings Ordinance to tighten regulation of large-scale building maintenance works, with the Development Bureau submitting its proposals to the Legislative Council on November 20. Works on buildings of four storeys or more covered by scaffolding to a certain extent will become a new standalone category of large-scale building maintenance works, which must be coordinated by an Authorized Person and approved by the Buildings Department before work can start, and may only be undertaken by registered general building contractors or Class I minor works contractors. The proposals also separate inspection from supervision to break conflicts of interest, and raise the maximum penalty for permitting defective materials, breaching prescribed material standards or seriously deviating from plans to a HK$3 million fine and three years' jail, up from HK$1 million; starting work without a permit will carry up to HK$2 million and two years' jail. The Legislative Council's Panel on Development will discuss the proposals on Tuesday (November 24), and the bureau aims to table the bill in January next year and complete legislation by mid-year.

summary.en: The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in San Francisco is broadening its reach in showcasing Hong Kong cinema through institutional partnerships with the University of San Francisco and the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive, connecting Hong Kong films with university and museum communities across the San Francisco Bay Area. The inaugural Hong Kong Films in Focus series opened at the University of San Francisco on November 9 (San Francisco time) with a screening of "The Last Dance", Hong Kong's all-time highest-grossing domestic film, attracting more than 50 students and community members. The Berkeley Art Museum's "Hong Kong Cinema: Rarities and Restorations" runs from October 23 to November 28, screening nine films spanning more than three decades of Hong Kong cinema, from romance to wuxia. Director of the office, DC Cheung, said that over the past year it has organised or supported 13 film festivals, community screenings and retrospectives in California, Colorado, Hawaii and Washington to promote Hong Kong culture.

summary.en: Bitcoin has fallen below US$58,000 to its lowest since September 2024, dropping about 6 per cent in a day and touching an intraday low of about US$57,778. The sell-off came as artificial-intelligence shares plunged, with the Nasdaq down about 5 per cent, and as Federal Reserve policymakers raised the prospect of larger interest-rate hikes to fight stubborn inflation. Ether fell about 7 per cent to around US$1,622, while XRP, Solana and BNB lost about 5 to 6 per cent. About US$1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions were wiped out in 24 hours, and US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds saw US$582 million in net outflows on Thursday, including a record US$541.1 million redemption from BlackRock's IBIT fund. Bitcoin is down about 25 per cent in November, on track for its worst month since June 2022 and a seventh straight weekly loss, and has fallen more than 50 per cent from its record above US$126,000 set in October 2025.

summary.en: Wan Chai's Hung Shing Temple, built between 1847 and 1852, has been formally gazetted as a declared monument in October 2026 after standing for nearly 180 years in the heart of the busy district. The temple is dedicated to Hung Shing, the god of the South Sea widely worshipped by fishermen and seafarers, and was originally built on the Hong Kong Island coastline; the streets opposite, Tai Wong Street East and West, are named after the temple's nickname 'Tai Wong'. As reclamation and urban development turned the sea in front of the temple into busy streets, the temple has become a historical marker quietly recording the changing Wan Chai coastline. It is also a rare Lingnan architectural gem, built to a traditional one-hall, three-bay layout with a porch that opens from both sides, granite columns topped with human figures, a stone balustrade carved with twin dragons playing with a pearl, and a 1909 Shiwan ceramic ridge depicting the heroine Fan Lihua. Most remarkably, the temple was built directly against a natural rock, its walls following the rock's uneven surface, a temple-and-rock structure that is rare among Hong Kong temples. Managed by Tung Wah Group of Hospitals, the temple now runs workshops, public talks and guided heritage tours to bring traditional temples closer to younger generations.
summary.zh_hans: 湾仔皇后大道东闹市一隅的洪圣古庙建于1847年至1852年，至今近180年历史，政府今年10月正式刊宪将其列为法定古迹。古庙主神洪圣是渔民和海上商旅敬拜的南海之神，最初建于香港岛海岸线，对面的大王东街和大王西街正是以古庙别名「大王」命名；随填海和城市发展，庙前碧海已化作繁华街道，古庙犹如历史坐标，默默纪录湾仔海岸线变迁。庙宇是罕见的岭南建筑瑰宝，采用传统「一进三开间」布局，门廊两侧进出设计本地少见，屋顶保存1909年烧制、描绘樊梨花故事的石湾陶脊；最特别的是古庙直接依附天然巨岩兴建，墙身倚岩石高低不平的表面而建，这种庙岩共生的结构在香港庙宇相当罕见。古庙由东华三院管理，近年透过工作坊、公众讲座和文化导赏路线，拉近传统庙宇与年轻一代的距离。

summary.en: The Election Committee subsector ordinary election will be held tomorrow. summary.en: The government plans to criminalise bid-rigging in building maintenance works. Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Yau Ying-wah said bid-rigging in building maintenance is serious and targeted legislation is needed immediately, adding that other serious bid-rigging could be covered later but the overall business environment must be balanced. The Bar Association earlier said it must be clarified whether the leniency mechanism under the Competition Ordinance would still apply in criminal prosecutions, and whether whistleblowers who report to the Competition Commission would be protected. Yau said those considerations are not ruled out but are not straightforward and will depend on the circumstances and the Department of Justice's advice.
